rv.q: This time, everything about the show is far subtler, more balanced and far richer in nuance.
Arden's production, at once intimate and epic, comes through beautifully nonetheless on the larger stage.
Directed to a fine, piercing point by Michael Arden, it all feels far too familiar.
“Parade” is the best touring musical of the year so far, but the run is short.
Parade is an important and touching musical that is as breathtaking and mysterious as it is shocking.
And that case is further bolstered by the transfixing, first-rate production that has arrived at the Emerson Colonial Theatre.
Michael Arden’s powerful Tony-Award-winning revival, now on tour and making its stop at Los Angeles’ Ahmanson Theatre, proves how tragically timely this true story still feels.
These are the moments where song and story most aptly collide, though a strong book from playwright Alfred Uhry (“Driving Miss Daisy”) ensures the show never steers far off-course.
Coming at a time when the issues it raises are, as the show notes, “ongoing,” it puts a palpably human touch on issues that are too often merely rhetorical.
His performance takes it from a grim catalogue of horrific injustice to a story with humanity at its heart.
It may not necessarily evoke the most intense emotion, but it’s a valuable education, at the theater, at that!
It’s a deeply moving, gorgeously performed piece of theatre that stays with you long after the final curtain falls.
The title Parade belies the historical significance, power, and vital message of this musical tragedy.

cn.t: Critics praise this timely revival of "Parade" for its powerful, haunting resonance and lush score, though the heavy subject matter makes it more emotionally engaging than entertaining.

vr.q: The whole cast is phenomenal. Brilliant, nuanced performances.
I cannot recommend going to see this enough.
